opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Category maxima: New Projects and Commissions £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications £5,000; Long-Term Research £20,000; Research and Travel £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating in a non-profit capacity for at least 12 months) for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research categories. Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply to the Research and Travel category. Individuals independently wishing to develop their own artistic practice are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories cover exhibitions, catalogues, commissions, acquisitions, conservation, conferences, publications and long-term research. Applications considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600; Europe up to £700; Rest of world up to £1,000, plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture. Artist Research Fellowships support artists developing their practice through research. Senior Fellowships for established scholars (six weeks).
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the research facilities at the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications for 2026/27 are closed; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation £250 cash prize; MA dissertation £250 cash prize; plus £50 of Institute publications

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines who submitted a dissertation within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, open to BA and MA students at UK universities. The 2025 prize deadline has passed; submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
